To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
(1) fracture clustering is an important feature of crystalline basement rock masses and (2) the spatial clustering of the fractures in the crystalline basement rocks is depth dependent.

(i) the fracture network of the crystalline basement rocks is highly heterogeneous and clustered; (ii) the fracture density and clustering are depth dependent; (iii) the fracture density decreases with depth and the fracture spacing increases; (iv) the fracture density, fracture spacing and fracture clustering are highly variable in the vertical direction.
The clustering of fractures in crystalline basement rocks is depth dependent and that this clustering has an impact on the hydraulic and mechanical properties of the rock.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following aspects: (1) the characterization of the fracture clustering in a crystalline basement rock mass using fracture image logs, (2) the development of a method to determine the spatial clustering from the line samples, and (3) the application of the developed method to the characterization of a fractured crystalline basement rock.
the development of a novel methodology to analyze fracture image logs and core data, which allows the characterization of the spatial distribution of fractures in three dimensions.
the development and application of novel methods for the characterization of the spatial distribution of fractures in crystalline basement rocks.
